# This note — AI agent guide

This folder is one note in a FigixNote vault. Its human-readable title lives
in `meta.json`'s `title` field, not in this folder's name (`note_<uuid>`). If
you can see the vault root, check `INDEX.md` there for the title -> folder
map.

## Files

- `pages.json` — this note's pages, in display order: `[{ "id": "page_xxx",
  "title": "1" }, ...]`. A note always has at least one page. `title` is
  whatever the user renamed the page to (or the default `"1"`, `"2"`, ...) —
  it is NOT a file name.
- `pages/<id>.md` — one page's text per file (`id` matches a `pages.json`
  entry's `id`, e.g. `pages/page_xxx.md`). Edit these freely; each is plain
  Markdown plus one convention, below. This is where the note's actual
  content lives.
- `assets/` — images/video/3D models referenced from any page's markdown.
  Shared across every page in this note (not per-page). Reference a file
  with a path relative to this note folder, e.g. `assets/img_xxx.png`.
- `meta.json`, `strokes.json`, `thumbnail.png` — app-owned state (title,
  timestamps, which page was last open; hand-drawn canvas strokes; the card
  preview image). Don't hand-edit these: the app overwrites them on its own
  schedule, and a malformed `strokes.json` or `meta.json` can make the note
  fail to open.
- `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (this file) — regenerated by the app; edits are
  overwritten.

## Adding a page by hand

Prefer the app's own "새 페이지" button when possible. If you do need to add
one directly: write the new page's Markdown to `pages/<new-id>.md` (any
unique id, e.g. `page_` followed by a random string, to stay consistent with
the app's own ids) and append `{ "id": "<new-id>", "title": "<name>" }` to
the array in `pages.json`. Never remove the last remaining page — a note
with zero pages is invalid.

## Footnote-media convention in a page's markdown

Media is attached to the text via a Markdown footnote pair, not an inline
`![]()`:

    Some sentence with an idea.[^3]

    [^3]: ![optional alt text](assets/img_xxx.png)

- The reference `[^3]` can go anywhere in the body; its matching
  `[^3]: ![...](...)` definition is conventionally collected at the end of
  the file.
- The definition's path decides how it renders: an image extension renders
  as an image, video extensions (`.mp4`, `.webm`, `.mov`, ...) as video, 3D
  model extensions (`.glb`, `.gltf`, `.fbx`) as an embedded viewer, and a
  `youtube.com`/`youtu.be` URL as an embedded player — same `[^n]: ![]()`
  syntax in every case, only the path/extension changes.
- Footnote ids only need to be unique within their own page — two different
  pages can each have their own `[^1]`. They don't need to stay sequential
  or gap-free either; the app only renumbers them on an explicit user
  action, never automatically. Reusing the next unused integer is enough.
- Always add or remove a reference and its definition together, within the
  same page. One without the other is an "orphan" that the app's cleanup
  action silently deletes the next time a user runs it.
